question.problem: Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-9) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -5) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(\lambda -5)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =5,\,2,\,-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, writing the eigenvalues in descending order, we obtain the diagonal matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The corresponding quadratic form after a change of variables is

$$
5{y}_{1}^{2}+2{y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{3}^{2}.
$$
